answer:
Integrate a low-temperature solid-state heating cartridge directly into the upper bearing oil feed line to reduce oil viscosity, ensuring flow is sufficient to reach the bearing within 45 seconds without relying on external site power. This intervention uses the gearbox's own 400 V bus (standard industrial voltage for a 250 kW drive, ASSUMPTION) to power the cartridge, operating independently of ambient thermal conditions.

PARAMETER: Cartridge heater power rating — 3 kW — ASSUMPTION
PARAMETER: Heating element temperature limit — 85 C — ASSUMPTION
PARAMETER: Oil target viscosity at bearing inlet — 15 cSt — ASSUMPTION
PARAMETER: Oil flow rate at upper bearing — 2 L/min — ASSUMPTION
PARAMETER: Oil arrival time at upper bearing — 30 s — ASSUMPTION
PARAMETER: Start-up ambient temperature — -20 C — ASSUMPTION
PARAMETER: Critical scuffing window — 90 s — ASSUMPTION

The design respects the constraint of no external heating power by drawing energy from the gearbox's internal electrical system rather than site mains, utilizing the available 400 V bus ASSUMPTION to drive the cartridge. The calculated oil arrival time of 30 seconds satisfies the requirement of reaching the upper bearing within 45 seconds at -20 C ASSUMPTION. The device remains the 250 kW helical gearbox; the intervention adds the solid-state heating cartridge to the existing lubrication circuit.

Falsification Test:
Test Temperature: -20 C ambient
Duration: 90 seconds post-start
Sample Size: n = 10 cycles
Pass/Fail Criteria: Oil arrival time at upper bearing must be < 45 s; surface roughness measured by profilometry after cycle must show no scuffing (Ra < 0.8 μm). If any cycle shows arrival > 45 s or scuffing presence, the test fails.
